ambiguities.evidence: Section 1.3 first says 'independent random variables X1, ..., XN' and later in the same calculation says 'as N → ∞'.
ambiguities.impact: A formal statement must choose a coherent family across N, naturally an infinite sequence whose first N entries form each sample, although that rebinding is implicit rather than written in this paragraph.
ambiguities.issue: The paragraph begins with notation for a finite family X₁, ..., X_N and then lets N tend to infinity without separately rebinding an infinite sequence.

contract_plain_english: For independent, identically distributed real random variables with one fixed finite variance σ², the variance of the average of the first N variables is σ²/N and therefore tends to zero as N grows.

source_evidence.anchor: Var(X1 + · · · + XN) = Var(X1) + · · · + Var(XN) holds for any independent random variables X1, ..., XN
source_evidence.location: PDF pages 4-5; printed pages 8-9; Section 1.3 opening
source_evidence.observation: Independence is the standing hypothesis for the variance calculation that precedes the sample-mean claim.

source_evidence.anchor: If, furthermore, Xi have the same distribution with mean µ and variance σ²
source_evidence.location: PDF page 5; printed page 9; sentence immediately preceding Equation (1.5)
source_evidence.observation: The variables additionally have one common distribution, common mean µ, and common variance σ².

source_evidence.anchor: Var((1/N) sum from i=1 to N of Xi) = σ²/N
source_evidence.observation: The exact variance of the sample mean is σ²/N, providing the quantitative basis for the limit.

source_evidence.anchor: Thus, the variance of the sample mean ... shrinks to zero as N → ∞
source_evidence.location: PDF page 5; printed page 9; paragraph after Equation (1.5)
source_evidence.observation: The asserted conclusion is that the variance of the normalized sample mean converges to zero as the sample size tends to infinity.

source_evidence.anchor: Var(X) = E(X − E X)²; X : Ω → R
source_evidence.location: PDF page 1; printed page 5; Section 1.1 opening and footnote 1
source_evidence.observation: Random variables are real-valued functions on a probability space, and variance is defined as the expected squared centered value.

binders: A sequence X₁, X₂, ... of real-valued random variables on a common probability space.
A common mean µ and a fixed finite common variance σ².
A positive integer sample size N tending to infinity through the positive integers.
definitions_and_conventions: The sample mean is M_N = (1/N) ∑_{i=1}^N Xᵢ.
hypotheses: The random variables have the same distribution.
Each Xᵢ has mean µ and variance σ².
implicit_context: All variables being added are defined on one probability space.
The independence hypothesis is inherited from the immediately preceding variance-sum sentence.
The common-distribution and common-moment hypotheses are introduced by the phrase 'If, furthermore'.
The common variance is finite and fixed rather than depending on N, as required by σ²/N → 0.

details: The convergent quantity is the real-valued variance of the sample mean, not the sample mean random variable itself.
The surrounding exact identity gives the variance decay rate σ²/N.
The calculation uses both independence and identical distribution.
A finite common second moment is encoded by the common finite variance σ².

undebatable_constraints: The conclusion is convergence of the variance to zero.
The normalization is exactly 1/N applied to the sum of the first N variables.
Independence and identical distribution are inherited assumptions.
The variables have one fixed common finite variance σ².
The limit is taken as the positive integer N tends to infinity.
This claim does not assert almost-sure, in-probability, or distributional convergence of the sample mean itself.
